subject.title: fix: full release validation avoids embedded-agent shard stalls

question: Should the release/CI owner accept the 660-second no-output window for frozen compatibility validation after the branch is refreshed onto current `main`?
rationale: The patch has direct hosted after-fix proof, but it deliberately changes the time before the release gate declares a silent frozen-target shard stalled; that operational tradeoff requires owner acceptance.

options.title: Rebase and land with refreshed proof
options.body: Refresh the branch onto current `main`, verify the scoped timeout ordering remains unchanged, and retain a successful final-head embedded-agent release-shard run.

options.title: Keep the shorter watchdog
options.body: Reject the longer outer watchdog and pursue a more granular progress signal or shard restructuring if release owners do not accept the added detection delay.

recommendation.title: Rebase and land with refreshed proof
recommendation.body: Refresh the branch onto current `main`, verify the scoped timeout ordering remains unchanged, and retain a successful final-head embedded-agent release-shard run.
